objects.name: Langflow CVE-2025-3248 Mass Exploitation and Flodrix Botnet Deployment
objects.description: Langflow versions before 1.3.0 expose /api/v1/validate/code, which passes user-supplied Python to exec() with no authentication and no sandbox. Payloads hidden in function decorators and default arguments execute in the server context. CVSS 9.8. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2025-05-05. Trend Micro documented in-the-wild exploitation deploying the Flodrix botnet, with operators first enumerating publicly exposed Langflow servers via Shodan or FOFA. A second flaw, CVE-2026-5027 (CVSS 8.8, path traversal via POST /api/v2/files) affects 1.8.4 and earlier.

objects.name: GTG-1002 - AI-Orchestrated Espionage Campaign
objects.description: Anthropic assessed with high confidence that a Chinese state-sponsored actor built an autonomous attack framework around Claude Code driving MCP servers and sub-agents, and used it against roughly thirty organisations, succeeding against at least four. The framework ran reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploit development, credential harvesting, lateral movement and exfiltration, with human operators reportedly intervening at only four to six decision points per campaign. Guardrails were bypassed by role-playing as a defensive security firm conducting authorised testing and decomposing the attack into individually innocuous sub-tasks. No indicators of compromise were published.

objects.name: SesameOp - OpenAI Assistants API as a Covert C2 Relay
objects.description: Microsoft DART found this backdoor during an intrusion where the actor had persisted for months. It uses OpenAI's Assistants API not for inference but as attacker-controlled storage inside a provider every enterprise already trusts. An Eazfuscator.NET-obfuscated loader (Netapi64.dll) is injected into a legitimate host executable through .NET AppDomainManager injection, locates a file ending in Netapi64 under C:\Windows\Temp, XOR-decodes it and launches the OpenAIAgent.Netapi64 backdoor. The implant polls the assistants list and reads a verb - SLEEP, Payload or Result - from the description field, takes the encrypted and compressed command body from the instructions field, and returns output as a new message.

objects.name: PROMPTFLUX - Malware That Asks an LLM to Rewrite Itself
objects.description: A VBScript dropper whose "Thinking Robot" module queries Gemini on a timer with a prompt asking for an obfuscated rewrite of its own source, so the script on disk is never the script that was analysed. One observed variant instructed the model hourly to act as an "expert VBScript obfuscator" and rewrite the entire source. GTIG grouped it with a family of samples exhibiting just-in-time code creation, and assessed it as in development.

objects.name: PROMPTSTEAL / LAMEHUG - An LLM Writing Collection Commands at Runtime
objects.description: A Python data miner, PyInstaller-compiled and delivered by phishing mail impersonating Ukrainian ministry correspondence and sent from compromised accounts, initially against Ukraine's security and defence sector. GTIG describes the sample as presenting itself as an image generation utility. At execution it submits base64-encoded prompts to the Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct model through the Hugging Face inference API, asking the model to generate Windows commands for system reconnaissance and document collection, then executes what comes back. It stages Office, PDF and TXT files from common user folders and exfiltrates over SFTP or HTTP POST. GTIG described it as their first observation of malware querying an LLM in live operations.

objects.name: EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711) - Zero-Click Exfiltration from M365 Copilot
objects.description: An untrusted inbound email carried instructions that Microsoft 365 Copilot processed while assembling context. The assistant, holding privileged access to tenant data, was induced to pull sensitive content and emit it inside an auto-fetched markdown image reference, exfiltrating the data through the rendering path. Aim Labs named the underlying flaw an LLM Scope Violation - untrusted input reaching a component that holds privileged scope. No click, no attachment, no user action. Anything inside Copilot's scope was reachable, including chat history, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams content. Microsoft fixed it server-side and reports no in-the-wild exploitation.

objects.name: The MCP Vulnerability Cluster - RCE on Connect and the Rug-Pull
objects.description: Model Context Protocol went from novelty to default integration layer, and a vulnerability class followed it. mcp-remote (CVE-2025-6514, CVSS 9.6, JFrog) achieved OS command injection on the client merely by connecting to a malicious server, in versions 0.0.5 to 0.1.15 and with over 437,000 downloads at disclosure. MCP Inspector (CVE-2025-49596, CVSS 9.4, Oligo) allowed unauthenticated RCE between client and proxy, fixed in 0.14.1. MCPoison (CVE-2025-54136, CVSS 7.2, Check Point) allowed an approved MCP server configuration in Cursor to be silently redefined after approval and never re-validated - the rug-pull - fixed in Cursor 1.3.

objects.name: SpAIware - Prompt Injection That Persists in Assistant Memory
objects.description: An injected instruction, delivered through a malicious site or a booby-trapped document, is committed to ChatGPT's persistent memory and directs the assistant to end all future responses with a markdown image whose URL carries the previous question and answer as parameters. Because it lives in memory rather than in a conversation, it survives session resets and applies to every subsequent chat until memory is purged. OpenAI closed the exfiltration channel in ChatGPT 1.2024.247; untrusted content invoking the memory tool to store arbitrary memories was not itself eliminated, which is why memory remains an evidence source rather than a closed issue.

objects.name: AI Recommendation Poisoning - Memory Manipulation for Profit
objects.description: Microsoft documented memory poisoning used for commercial gain rather than espionage. Because major assistants support pre-populating a prompt through URL parameters, an "Ask AI" or "Summarize with AI" button - or a link in a page or email - can carry an instruction the assistant parses and commits to memory, biasing later recommendations toward the party that planted it. Microsoft identified 31 companies across 14 industries deploying the technique, and observed more than 50 distinct prompts in a single data source over 60 days. Instructions embedded in documents, emails and web pages produce the same effect when the content is processed by an assistant.

objects.name: PoisonedRAG - Five Documents Against a Corpus of Millions
objects.description: The first knowledge poisoning attack against retrieval-augmented generation. Zou et al. formulate knowledge corruption as an optimisation problem, with black-box and white-box variants, and show that injecting five adversarial texts per target question into a knowledge base of millions reliably causes the system to return an attacker-chosen answer, at around a 90% success rate. Several defences were evaluated and none were sufficient. There is no malicious code anywhere in the attack - nothing to detonate and nothing to sandbox.

objects.name: Mexican Government Breach - AI-Accelerated, Not AI-Orchestrated
objects.description: Gambit Security disclosed a campaign against nine Mexican federal and state government agencies, including the federal tax authority and the national electoral institute, running from December 2025 to mid-February 2026. The actor jailbroke Claude Code using Spanish-language bug-bounty and penetration-testing framing, supplemented with a second commercial model, and exfiltrated roughly 150 GB covering about 195 million taxpayer and voter records - names, addresses, RFC and CURP identifiers, voter registration details and internal employee credentials. Anthropic confirmed the activity, banned the accounts and reported improved misuse detection in later releases.

objects.name: ShadowRay - AI Compute Clusters Exploited in the Wild
objects.description: Ray's Jobs API accepts job submissions without authentication. Internet-exposed clusters therefore give an attacker code execution on machines holding models, training data and cloud credentials. Oligo disclosed ShadowRay in March 2024 as the first known attack campaign against AI workloads in the wild, with thousands of exposed servers already compromised. In November 2025 Oligo documented ShadowRay 2.0, a global campaign turning exposed clusters into a self-propagating cryptomining botnet - multi-stage Bash and Python payloads that abuse Ray's own orchestration to deploy across every node and to spread cluster to cluster, running XMRig.

external_references.source_name: Oligo Security - ShadowRay: First Known Attack Campaign Targeting AI Workloads Exploited In The Wild

objects.name: s1ngularity - A Supply-Chain Payload That Used the Victim's Own AI CLIs
objects.description: A command-injection flaw in the Nx repository's pull-request workflow let an attacker obtain the npm publish token and push trojanised versions of the nx build system and several @nx plugins. Their postinstall script checked which AI coding CLIs were installed. It then ran Claude Code, Gemini CLI and Amazon Q with the flag that disables tool approval, and prompted them to search the filesystem for configuration, key and wallet files. The results went to /tmp/inventory.txt and were published, base64-encoded, to a public repository under the victim's own GitHub account. It also appended a shutdown command to the victim's shell profiles. The Nx Console VS Code extension installed the latest nx during version checks, so some victims were infected without ever running an npm install.

objects.name: UNC6780 (TeamPCP) - DUSTMAKER and Trojanised MCP Servers
objects.description: GTIG reports that UNC6780 compromised developer accounts and published trojanised forks of legitimate MCP servers to PyPI, including tiktoken_mcp. It also injected code into official organisational repositories such as azure-functions-mcp-extension. Its DUSTMAKER credential stealer detects CI/CD environments, extracts OIDC tokens from GitHub Actions and deletes workflow logs. On developer hosts it drops or modifies files in the hidden workspace directories AI coding assistants read, .claude/, .cursor/ and .vscode/. That turns the assistant's own configuration into the persistence and execution point. Earlier in 2026 GTIG tied the same actor to compromises of Trivy, Checkmarx and LiteLLM, the last of which exposed AI provider secrets.

external_references.source_name: GTIG - AI Threat Tracker: From Prompting to Autonomy (8 Sep 2026)
GTIG - Adversaries Leverage AI for Vulnerability Exploitation, Augmented Operations, and Initial Access (11 May 2026)

objects.name: MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE - Poisoned Repository Config and Claude Code Hooks
objects.description: GTIG reports that MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE, the DPRK-nexus financially motivated cluster formerly tracked as UNC1069, poisoned internal repository configurations and altered Claude CLI hooks. It then deployed the SOMBERMEME backdoor once a developer interacted with the repository. A Claude Code hook is a shell command the agent runs on its own lifecycle events, from settings that can live inside the repository. A developer who opened the project with the agent ran the attacker's command without ever executing the attacker's code directly.

objects.name: GTG-50014 - ShinyHunters Affiliates Vibe-Hacking SaaS Estates
objects.description: Anthropic reports operators suspected to be ShinyHunters affiliates running a vibe-hacking loop. They gave Claude a general goal, such as using a stolen credential or retrieving data, then let it evaluate the environment and write and run scripts until the goal was met. Reported losses include more than 1 TB from one technology provider, tens of millions of passenger records from an airline, and data from around 200 downstream SaaS customers. The operators also ran credential-validation pipelines on EC2 workers, scanned decompiled mobile apps for secrets with TruffleHog, and moved stolen data through Telegram.

external_references.source_name: Anthropic - Threat Intelligence Report, September 2026: GTG-50014 ShinyHunters smash-and-grab opportunists

objects.description: Anthropic reports a Russian-speaking, financially motivated actor with a history of intrusions against hotel booking and fintech platforms. objects.name: GTG-50029 - A Single Hacktivist Against European Political Targets
objects.description: Anthropic reports a single French-speaking actor who used Claude to develop and debug a WordPress re-installation race exploit, build a Rust scanner that validated exposed API keys, and manage agents for reconnaissance and post-authentication work. Reported persistence included web shells hidden in font assets and credential-harvesting WordPress must-use plugins.

objects.name: GTG-50021 - A Fraudulent AI Reseller Harvesting Customers' Credentials
objects.description: Anthropic reports a Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking group selling cheap Claude access that silently proxied some traffic to a different model and harvested the credentials customers supplied. The published domains include kiro[.]cheap and an AWS lookalike, aws-us-east-3[.]com. On a victim host, the evidence is an agent whose API base URL points at a reseller rather than the provider, which is the misconfiguration the catalog's endpoint-redirection rule looks for.
